subject: All
finding: Unnecessary formula panels and forced examples
evidence: 237 example formula lists cleared; 9 examples removed; 13 authored explanation updates. Full content snapshot and per-change backup retained.
recommendation: Keep formula and example decisions independent and tied to a stable outcome identifier. Never reintroduce a formula simply because the subject is mathematical.

subject: Maths
status: Applied to local DB and source
finding: Incorrect Foundation exclusions
evidence: The validator previously rejected all compound interest, inverse proportion and exact trigonometric values at Foundation.
recommendation: Retain the corrected Foundation scope and both added warranted examples. Maintain exact specification mapping rather than blanket exclusions.

subject: Science
finding: 52 stale question-bank labels across Maths and Science
evidence: All 52 stale labels resolved: 12 percentage questions mapped to the current outcome and 40 Science questions rewritten. Higher mole/equilibrium teaching remains in the dedicated Higher topic. Arithmetic errors in two of the percentage tasks were also corrected.
recommendation: Keep stable outcome identifiers and validate question metadata whenever the catalogue changes; complete board-specific statement mapping.

subject: Science
status: Core/Higher explanation selection implemented and tested
finding: Higher material in shared Foundation/Higher teaching
evidence: Shared explanations store a separate Higher extension. API, preview and narration choose the learner tier before presenting the text. Foundation no longer receives the identified inverse-square, strong/weak-acid and other Higher extensions.
recommendation: Continue exact board/outcome mapping and subject review; the tier selector is a safeguard, not proof that every statement is correctly classified.

subject: Science
status: Identified content corrected locally; full specification mapping remains
finding: Separate Chemistry teaching in Combined Science
evidence: The identified separate-Chemistry ion-test examples and unnecessary alkene formula recall were removed or rewritten for the Combined pathway.
recommendation: Map explicitly to AQA 8464 and Edexcel 1SC0 statement IDs. Retain required gas tests and hydrocarbon/cracking content; keep separate-Chemistry ion tests and unnecessary alkene formula recall out of the AQA Combined pathway.

subject: History
finding: Ancient History units assigned to GCSE History qualifications
evidence: Greece and Persia, Alexander the Great, Rome and its Neighbours, and Hannibal and the Second Punic War are assigned AQA 8145/Edexcel 1HI0 through blanket board metadata.
recommendation: Move these four units to an explicitly optional enrichment pathway or separately support Ancient History with its own qualification/options. Do not present them as required AQA 8145 or Edexcel 1HI0 units.

subject: History
status: Named examples and question-bank tasks corrected locally
finding: Historical explanation replaced by arithmetic
evidence: The initial cleanup removed the WW1 importance score. This batch rewrote ten y10-history-change-across-time rate questions and y8-history-transatlantic-slavery-and-empire/practice-4-core-core using qualitative analysis. Invented teaching scenarios are explicitly labelled fictional.
recommendation: Use historical evidence, causation, continuity, significance and substantiated judgement. Quantitative evidence may support an argument, but should not replace the stated historical skill.

subject: English
status: Named task corrected; generation prompt improved
finding: English tasks can become calculation exercises
evidence: y10-english-spoken/practice-9-AQA-core now assesses sequencing ideas, audience signposting and a closing request. Generation guidance explicitly avoids replacing English objectives with arithmetic.
recommendation: Assess ordering ideas, audience, signposting and delivery. Keep useful punctuation demonstrations and model paragraphs. Do not force step-by-step numerical solutions or formula panels into literary or rhetorical work.

subject: English / History / Geography
finding: Board selection does not select texts, historical options or case studies
evidence: Generic topics such as Shakespeare, The 19th-century Novel, British Society in Depth and Case Studies and Exam Skills have no exact school-selected text/option in the curriculum metadata.
recommendation: Add qualification version, exam series, paper/component, option, set text/anthology and case-study identifiers to enrolment and content. Build coverage against the selected course rather than a generic subject label.

subject: All GCSE subjects
finding: Uniform 1–6-mark exam format cannot represent full GCSE demand
evidence: questionBank.js requests one creditworthy point per mark and clamps all exam questions to six marks. This cannot represent the extended essays and level-based marking used in GCSE English and History.
recommendation: Label existing short items as short practice. Add board/paper-specific question types, maximum marks, assessment objectives and level-based rubrics before claiming full exam preparation.

subject: Maths / Design & Technology
finding: Questions missing necessary input data
evidence: The Maths comparison example now supplies both datasets. The DT energy task states its assumptions and electricity tariff, has six creditworthy marking points, corrects annual cost to £21,880 and explains why unknown capital costs prevent a full first-year cost comparison.
recommendation: Supply every input, extract, diagram or dataset in the question itself. Independently solve from the prompt only before approving a row.

subject: Science
status: Applied to local DB and source
finding: Removing a formula list does not cure an irrelevant example
evidence: The identified immune-response example was rewritten without antibody-concentration arithmetic or post-GCSE signalling detail.
recommendation: Replace with an appropriate GCSE explanation of pathogens, antibodies, vaccination and a faster secondary response; remove contrived calculations and unnecessary post-GCSE mechanisms.

subject: Geography
status: Confirmed coverage gap in explicit outcomes
finding: KS3 regional coverage is incomplete
evidence: KS3 outcomes cover West Africa and South Asia, but do not explicitly teach Russia, the Middle East or China.
recommendation: Add locational knowledge and human/physical comparisons for these required regions, with map activities; retain the existing African and Asian regional studies.

subject: Science
finding: KS3 Science has weak explicit coverage of some required strands
evidence: No explicit Science outcomes for the rock cycle/Earth structure or recreational-drug effects; rocks appear in Geography and nutrition partly in Design & Technology.
recommendation: Add Science outcomes or explicit cross-subject mappings, with evidence of learning. Check nutrition/deficiency, breathing/health, static electricity and domestic-energy costs against the complete KS3 programme.

subject: English
finding: Required reading breadth is not evidenced by topic names
evidence: Two KS3 Shakespeare topic labels do not record which two whole plays are studied; author and independent-reading coverage is not tracked.
recommendation: Record two Shakespeare plays, whole-book reading, world literature and two authors studied in depth per year; distinguish a skill lesson from evidence that a whole text has been studied.

subject: Computing
finding: Practical programming and specification versions need explicit evidence
evidence: Practical programming and specification-version evidence remain necessary. The identified logarithmic/Big-O tasks have been removed or rewritten; repaired Python answers preserve indentation and executable syntax.
recommendation: Require practical work in two languages, at least one textual; keep GCSE algorithm comparison informal; map SQL/networking and other board differences to the correct specification version.

subject: Design & Technology / Geography / Science
finding: Text answers cannot evidence all practical requirements
evidence: The question generator prohibits drawings, construction and practical outputs. DT has design/make outcomes; Geography requires fieldwork; Science has required practicals.
recommendation: Add practical-task records, safe teacher-led instructions, portfolio/diagram uploads and suitable rubrics. Preserve relevant quantitative work: AQA DT assesses mathematics and science as well as design.

subject: All
finding: Coverage and scope validators gave misleading assurance
evidence: Coverage previously requested every outcome's example, both tiers even on single-tier topics, and the obsolete any key for KS3 banks. Pruning treated SE map labels as standard error and banned named sampling across subjects.
recommendation: Use live content-key and outcome policies for coverage. Treat heuristic hits as candidates; retain legitimate Geography sampling and verify context before deleting anything.

subject: All
finding: Most rows have no recorded approval
evidence: Current local review flags: 8796 pending and 2 pre-existing approved. All 8798 current payloads have a hash-matched nano review. No teacher approval was assigned by this work.
recommendation: Track reviewer, date, evidence, specification reference and content hash. Model review should create a review task, never automatically approve or publish a row.

subject: All
finding: Outcome positions are unstable content identifiers
evidence: Examples use example-index-tier keys while question banks retain old outcome labels after curriculum edits.
recommendation: Introduce immutable outcome IDs and content revision IDs; migrate indexed rows explicitly, invalidate related narration and run coverage/integrity checks after every curriculum edit.

subject: Geography
finding: Unsupported comparison of disaster response speed
evidence: The disaster-response question now identifies fictional scenarios, compares the actual milestones and explicitly avoids claiming one evacuation or recovery was faster.
recommendation: Compare each stated milestone accurately and explain the limits of comparing different response measures. Do not adopt Nano's alternative claim that earthquake evacuation took 25 minutes: that was team arrival.

subject: All
status: Model flags adjudicated; qualified subject review remains
finding: Heuristic anomalies need contextual decisions
evidence: 0 current model suggestions remain unadjudicated, alongside 801 heuristic findings. Neither number is a confirmed defect count. Exact-hash retained decisions document rejected model suggestions.
recommendation: Check these against their full payloads. Do not equate alternative mark-scheme points with wrong totals, supplied extracts with missing extracts, or the same valid example at two tiers with an error.

subject: Computing / Science / Maths / Geography
status: Corrections applied locally; further review tracked
finding: Additional demand, equation, arithmetic and stimulus errors
evidence: 854 backed-up editorial write operations across 813 distinct current records; 259 initial policy operations recorded separately. Current authored-explanation and editorial-source drift: 0.
recommendation: Use the generated report, applied-change ledger and outstanding-model-flags.json for current record-level evidence. Do not present automated review as 100% certification.
